issues.description: The problem statement and the template require Farm to initialize its internal ArrayList in a constructor with no arguments (i.e., a public no-arg constructor). The reference solution instead provides only a constructor with an int parameter (public Farm(int initialCapacity)) and does not include a no-arg constructor. This mismatch breaks the specified API (students and examples expect new Farm()) and can confuse or block students who implement/instantiate Farm according to the specification.
issues.suggestedFix: Provide a public no-argument constructor in Farm that initializes the animals list (e.g. public Farm() { this.animals = new ArrayList<>(); }). Alternatively, if an initial-capacity constructor is desired, also include the no-arg constructor and keep the int-parameter constructor as an overload so the class matches the problem specification and template/example usages.
